title: Review of the basics: ten minutes of conversation
why: This big review closes the basics: the present and its irregular verbs, partitives, possessives, object pronouns, the near future, depuis, venir de and the negatives, all used together in a real conversation. After it, you're ready to tackle the past tenses of level A2.

Talking about your life in the present

You now have everything you need for a real conversation: who you are, what you do, what you like and what you're going to do. This review puts it all together, with the traps English speakers fall into most often.

One present for everything

French has a single present: je travaille = I work, I'm working, I do work. No \"do\" in questions or negatives: Tu travailles ?, Je ne travaille pas. Remember the three regular groups and the big irregulars:

parlerfinirattendreallerfaire
jeparlefinisattendsvaisfais
tuparlesfinisattendsvasfais
il / elle / onparlefinitattendvafait
nousparlonsfinissonsattendonsallonsfaisons
vousparlezfinissezattendezallezfaites
ils / ellesparlentfinissentattendentvontfont

Where English uses another tense

  • depuis + present for something still going on: J'habite à Lille depuis cinq ans = I've lived in Lille for five years. Same with ça fait… que: Ça fait cinq ans que j'habite ici.
  • venir de + infinitive for something that has just happened: Je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived.
  • être en train de + infinitive to stress an action in progress: Je suis en train de cuisiner.
Ça fait trois ans que je travaille à l'hôpital.I've been working at the hospital for three years.

Don't translate \"I have lived\" word for word. If the action is still going on, French keeps the present: J'habite ici depuis deux ans. And remember avoir for age: J'ai trente ans, never je suis trente.

", "

Tastes, things and people

The article: le or du?

To talk about what you like in general, French uses le, la, les where English uses nothing: J'adore le fromage (I love cheese). To talk about an unspecified amount, it uses du, de la, de l', des: Je prends du fromage (I'm having some cheese). After a negative, all of them become de: Je n'ai pas de voiture.

J'aime le vin rouge, mais ce soir, je bois de l'eau.I like red wine, but tonight I'm drinking water.
Je ne mange jamais de viande.I never eat meat.

Possessives agree with the thing

Son frère = his brother or her brother; sa voiture = his car or her car. The possessive agrees with the noun that follows, not with the owner. Before a vowel, use mon, ton, son even for a feminine noun: mon amie Sarah.

Object pronouns before the verb

Tu connais Léa ? — Oui, je la connais. The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb, or before the infinitive when there is one: Je vais la voir demain.

The other negatives

NegativeMeaningExample
ne… jamaisneverJe ne bois jamais de café.
ne… plusno longer, not anymoreIl n'habite plus à Lyon.
ne… riennothingJe ne veux rien.
ne… personnenobodyJe ne connais personne ici.
ne… pas encorenot yetJe ne travaille pas encore.

One negative word per idea: Je ne veux rien = I don't want anything. Never add pas to jamais, plus, rien or personne.

", "

Plans, questions and keeping it going

The near future

Aller + infinitive: Je vais déménager, On va dîner chez Manon. The negative goes around aller: Je ne vais pas sortir. Markers: ce soir, demain, la semaine prochaine, dans deux jours.

Asking questions

Three registers: rising intonation (Tu viens ?), est-ce que (Est-ce que tu viens ?) and a few fixed inversions (Comment allez-vous ?). In casual speech, the question word often goes at the end: Tu habites où ?

To ask about…Question
workQu'est-ce que vous faites dans la vie ?
where someone livesTu habites où ? Depuis combien de temps ?
tastesTu aimes la cuisine indienne ?
plansQu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce week-end ?
familyTu as des frères et sœurs ?

Tu or vous?

At a dinner with friends of friends, people of your age will quickly say tu. With an older person you're meeting for the first time, start with vous and wait for On se tutoie ?

Keeping the conversation going

Answer, then bounce the question back: Et toi ? / Et vous ? Agree with moi aussi or moi non plus, link your ideas with parce que, mais, alors, d'abord, ensuite, and use the little expressions: d'accord, ça dépend, pas de souci.

—Je n'aime pas le froid. —Moi non plus ! Alors, cet hiver, je vais partir à Nice.—I don't like the cold. —Me neither! So this winter, I'm going to Nice.

Ten minutes of conversation is mostly questions. Prepare five questions you can always ask: job, city, family, tastes, plans.
